decisions.reason: Lit encryption and ownership-gated decryption do not change the selected IPFS protocol, Pinata provider, initial hosting role, or client-removability of the hosted copy.
The source explicitly says the reader experience remains unchanged; PDF.js, read-only default behavior, and the existing viewer entry points remain valid.
Ownership-gated decryption does not remove or alter the optional offline-download link, its label, or its presentation; the source does not specify a different download policy.
The source configures Lit-based ebook access but does not request any FAQ addition or revision.
The existing metadata requirement already points users to an ownership-gated viewer, and the Datil/Lit configuration does not invalidate or necessarily change that metadata reference.
The Lit network and ebook-gating implementation decision does not entail a change to the About page copy.
Verifying current Base ERC-721 ownership is compatible with book access transferring to a secondary buyer and does not change any recorded transfer semantics.
The ebook access-control implementation does not change referral commission amount, trigger, recipient, timing, limit, or payout behavior.
Lit-based ebook ownership verification does not change the Transak provider, fiat conversion, payment methods, automatic mint flow, or the requirement's deferred lifecycle status.
The source decision does not alter random ticket allocation when no referral code is supplied.
Lit's automatic ERC-721 ownership check for ebook decryption is distinct from SIWE authentication and does not change the wallet-authenticated flows or dashboard sign-in rule.
The ebook gating configuration has no entailed effect on landing-page hero structure, visual density, messaging prominence, or control clearance.
